title: Replaying a délibération's approval chain after the workflow has been edited is the iparapheur demo
content:
The integration is an iparapheur approval hook dispatching a typed operation per signature step. Per-step rather than per-document matters for a signature workflow: the sequence of who signed in what order is the artefact, not just the final signed state.

The destructive step is different from the one used elsewhere. Other demos in this corpus delete an instance, purge executions or prune history; this one edits the workflow definition and then replays a délibération's full approval chain. That is a subtler failure mode and a more common one — workflows are revised as rules change, and once the definition has moved on, a system that stores only the current process cannot reconstruct what the old one required.

The single lead is Libriciel SCOP in France, recorded as a 90-person SCOP publishing twelve open-source products, marked "2 · next". A cooperative publishing at that scale is the kind of partner for whom a co-maintained integration is plausible, and the French local-government context supplies the délibération use case directly.
